vulnerabilityReview.rationale: Reviewed by the sole maintainer for Hospital 1.4.5 on 2026-09-22 and accepted; the pinned source inputs and reviewed fingerprint are unchanged from the prior accepted review. The Debian snapshot moved from 20260803T000000Z to 20260912T000000Z, which is why this review exists: the reviewed-inputs fingerprint moved with it, so the 1.2.3 acceptance could not carry forward. The snapshot was advanced to obtain the patched libpcre2, after two fixable HIGH findings appeared against libpcre2-8-0 10.42-1 -- CVE-2026-86145, published 2026-09-05, and CVE-2026-89161, published 2026-09-11, two days after the 1.3.2 candidate was built. Both are fixed in 10.42-1+deb12u1. Advancing the snapshot alone would not have applied the fix, because no stage of this Dockerfile upgrades already-installed packages; libpcre2-8-0 is therefore named explicitly at the patched version beside bash-static, in the same exact-pin style every other package here uses. What the six-week advance actually changed was measured rather than assumed, by building both and comparing the embedded build records: postgresql-configure.txt and compiler.txt are byte-identical, so neither the configure flags nor the gcc/ld toolchain moved; of the 202 packages in builder-packages.txt exactly one moved, linux-libc-dev 6.1.177-1 to 6.1.187-1, which supplies kernel headers at compile time and is not linked into any shipped binary. No source component changed: PostgreSQL 17.11, zlib 1.3.2 and ACL 2.4.0 keep the same versions, URLs and SHA-256 checksums. The ACL tarball was fetched from both snapshots and confirmed byte-identical at e661131456d2708a01c614a0f400e11d7d1bfaeb6f3e74b75bb980b72f0161a3, so the archive move does not alter what is compiled. The pinned image set is unchanged from 1.2.3. Separately, google.golang.org/grpc moved 1.83.1 to 1.83.2 in the source-built Caddy binary. That clears CVE-2026-84445 and retires the 1.3.2-only exception, which itself required removal once grpc reached 1.83.2. Both rebuilt images were rescanned with Trivy 0.74.0: zero CRITICAL, zero fixable HIGH. The only remaining findings are the two unfixed libsystemd0/libudev1 reports of CVE-2026-16742, each carrying its own exact current-release exception. This acceptance remains limited to the recorded checksums and provenance, because Trivy does not vulnerability-map the source-built components. The 1.1.0 component findings are carried forward, not re-verified: that PostgreSQL 17.11 was the newest 17.x security release at 2026-08-13; that zlib 1.3.2 is the newest upstream release and CVE-2026-22184 does not apply to it, because that flaw affects the untgz contrib utility through 1.3.1.2 which 1.3.2 removed; and that ACL 2.4.0 falls outside the affected ranges for CVE-2026-54369 and CVE-2026-54370. The recorded fingerprint covers the components, the Debian snapshot, the configure flags, the embedded build records and the pinned images, so any later change to any of them forces a fresh review rather than another carry-forward. Carried forward to 1.4.1 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.1 changes no Dockerfile, no pinned package version, no Debian snapshot and no source component, so the reviewed-inputs fingerprint is unmoved and this acceptance applies to exactly the inputs it was written against. Carried forward again to 1.4.2 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.2 changes no Dockerfile, no pinned package version, no Debian snapshot and no source component, so the reviewed-inputs fingerprint is unmoved. Carried forward again to 1.4.3 on 2026-09-20: 1.4.3 changes no Dockerfile, no pinned package version, no Debian snapshot and no source component, so the reviewed-inputs fingerprint is unmoved. Carried forward again to 1.4.4 on 2026-09-21: no Dockerfile, pinned package version, Debian snapshot or source component of the reviewed inputs changed. Carried forward again to 1.4.5 on 2026-09-22: no Dockerfile, pinned package version, Debian snapshot or source component of the reviewed inputs changed.
